purpose: Raymarched liquid-glass blobs for TouchDesigner, one member of the liquid-glass family, with a companion tutorial.
choices_origin: Family brief from the user (supplied); this member's direction from the workflow brief; remaining details delegated by the user and inferred here. No questions were asked: the user delegated design choices within the brief.

answers.value: Universality first (any object, scene, camera, least wiring), then match to the four reference images (look, not shape).
Adjustable glass colour and reflection, translucency, opacity, overall glass style.
No dithering; continuous only.
12-style presets: a menu that loads editable values, plus an A/B morph.
Separate Refraction TOP and Reflection TOP where the route uses them.
TouchDesigner users new to GLSL.
TouchDesigner 2025.x, GLSL 4.60, macOS Apple Silicon.
Smooth-min blobs and capsules that drift, merge and split, optional droplets, raymarched in a GLSL MAT on a proxy bounding box, writing gl_FragDepth.

Procedural by default; optional Layout TOP (pixel i = x, y, z, radius) so a CHOP or Table DAT can drive it through CHOP to TOP. Chosen over the GLSL MAT Arrays page because its per-row parameter names are not documented.
A Box SOP of size 2 inside blobs_geo; blobs live in -1..1; scale the Geometry COMP to resize. Back faces are rendered so the camera may be inside the box.

answers.origin: user (count: the family brief asks for 12-style presets) + inference (content)
answers.value: Twelve presets: four matching the references, four variations (mercury, amber, frosted, soap film) and four adapted from the core study's looks of the same names (emerald bottle, rose quartz, oil slick, aqua jelly), each with its own blob shape. Presets include blob shape; Count and Droplets are fractional so they morph. Until verifier finding V1 (2026-11-02) this study shipped eight and recorded the count as an inference; that was a shortfall against the brief, not a free choice.
Analytic silhouette coverage, because Render TOP multisampling cannot smooth a raymarched edge inside the box.
A thin orange ring passing through the blobs, so depth sorting is visible; backdrop with a bold type band, checkerboard, logo tile and discs.
studies/liquid-glass-blobs/ (not examples/, which hold real native exports).
Verify and fix the 21 findings of two independent reviewers; the user delegated design choices within this brief; no questions asked.

answers.topic: blobs too big for the box
answers.value: Cut flat by the box walls (a flat glass face), not shrunk to fit: Radius keeps its meaning, and the README explains how to avoid the cut.
Keep its alpha: the covered share refracts, the uncovered share blends like zero-wiring mode, so both old behaviours are special cases.

Fold running time forward and back over an hour (no jump; the blobs reverse direction once an hour) rather than wrapping with a jump or adding a CHOP accumulator. Superseded in the family sync by the integrated drift clock (see below).
blobs_geo Draw Priority -1, set leniently; no Write depth toggle, because depth sorting is the main promise.

Plain relative paths (scene, demo_env, layout_top) with an empty default, so Reset to Default empties them. Changed in the family sync to the core's convention: the default is the demo node, Reset to Default restores it, clearing the text empties the field.

Apply the core's audit rounds 2-3 items (R1-R9) and the family merge items (C1-C9) that fit a depth-writing proxy box; take core code only from commit 6a58487; keep this study's own better mechanisms; no questions asked (design choices delegated).

Three integrated drift phases (layout, ripple, film) with the layout's wave speeds rounded to multiples of 1/128 so the layout repeats after 256 pi of phase. Each phase wraps without a jump. Only the blob layout loops exactly, every 256 pi / Speed s (38 min at 0.35); the ripple repeats every 20 pi / (0.4 + Speed) s (84 s) and the film swirl every 256 / (0.015 + 0.045 Speed) s (about 2.3 h), so the whole image does not repeat exactly. Replaces reversing once an hour.
A quarter of the gap between neighbouring colour samples, chosen with the core's B7 method against a 64-sample reference (the whole gap measured twice as far off as no level).

Flip V flips the screen UV and the measured vertical sign together: with measured screen orientation, flipping only the UV would mirror every vertical bend for an upside-down Refraction TOP. In the case the core's UV-only rule was written for, the result is identical.

answers.topic: family close G1: what Object size means here
answers.origin: supplied (family brief: universality first; the family rule in Liquid Glass Lit decisions.json, family_rule; the critic's G1 task: align or record why the box route differs) + inference (delegated)
answers.value: Supplied: Object size = the object's world radius over 1.45, for the scene-unit lengths and the ripple and film lookups through worldScale(); keep this study's look on its own demo. Inferred: (1) align the number: Fit = the box's radius (1 x the Geometry COMP's scale) over 1.45, default 1 / 1.45, the unscaled demo's fit, as Liquid Glass Flow chose for its radius-1 sphere; (2) keep the look on the demo by converting each preset's Backdrop distance and Frost x 1.45 and Tint density / 1.45 once, as Liquid Glass Prism did for its own looks, including the four looks adapted from the core (they were tuned on this demo, not copied); (3) the film, a colour pattern, follows the rule's lookup (x worldScale(), frequency / Object size) but keeps this study's 2.5 swirls per box radius instead of the family's 2.5 per Object size, because the family's count made Oil Slick's film spotty here (244/255 on 48,887 pixels); (4) the ripple stays in box units with the rest of the shape, because it moves the surface (silhouette, depth, path); (5) Fit reads the box blobs.frag marches, not the Box SOP's bounds.

decisions.question: Which film count should Blobs use?
decisions.what_changed: Nothing changed on the demo: the presets render as at c94e849 (0 to 1/255). The difference is with the family rule. The rule gives 2.5 film swirls per Object size. Blobs gives 2.5 per box radius, which is 2.5 / 1.45 = 1.724 per Object size (uFilm.w = 2.5 / (1.45 x Object size)). So its film bands are 1.45 times as wide as the rule's.

options.A: Keep 2.5 per box radius (in the code now). No code change.
options.B: Use the family's 2.5 per Object size: 1.45 times as many bands. Measured on the demo at time 3: Oil Slick 244/255 on 48,887 pixels over 8/255, Soap Bubbles 234 on 43,868, Prism Clear 135 on 28,667, Type Lens 62 on 6,913. On Oil Slick the finer noise cells show as round spots. Changes: the uFilm.w expression in study.json, the shader comment, the film tests, captures.

decisions.recommended_origin: inference (the look-acceptance round, 2026-11-02; the user has not answered)
decisions.why_recommended: The finer count looks spotty on Oil Slick (captures/review-look-decisions.png). Fit already makes the film follow any box size, so universality does not depend on this number. The reference image with rainbow bands shows thin, dense bands that neither count reproduces, so the references do not settle it.

decisions.question: Should the ripple follow Object size, like the core's ripples, or the box, like the blob shape?
decisions.what_changed: Nothing changed on the demo. Ripple and Ripple scale stay in box units: blobField() adds ripple(p) with p in box coordinates, and uMotion.z is Ripple scale with no Object size or worldScale(). In the core, Wobble scale is divided by Object size and its lookup multiplied by worldScale().

options.A: Keep box units (in the code now). The ripple moves the surface (the silhouette, the depth and the measured path), so it stays part of the shape, like Radius and Merge. No code change.
options.B: Follow the rule: Ripple scale counts ripples per Object size, as the core's Wobble scale does, with the presets' Ripple scale divided by 1.45 once so the demo keeps its look. Once Fit is pressed both give the same image. They differ only when Object size does not match the box (typed by hand, or a Geometry COMP scaled without pressing Fit): then the ripple count changes with Object size, as the core's does. Changes: ripple() in blobs.frag, uMotion in study.json, presets.json, the box-unit tests.

decisions.recommended_origin: inference (the look-acceptance round, 2026-11-02; the user has not answered)
decisions.why_recommended: Both give the same image whenever Fit is pressed, and A keeps every shape control in one unit.
